facts.text: Water at camp depends on the date: the 7,400-ft bench has none in late May and late June, so melt snow there, while by late July and August the lower 6,200-6,400-ft basin camps have running water.
In late June the side trail from Ingalls Creek up to the Sherpa basin is overgrown and blocked by fallen trees in places.
Ice axe and crampons (late May, when the basin and col are snow-covered)
Warm layer and wind shell (late June; the ridge stays in shade and windy until mid-morning)
The rock pitches are short, so a 50 m rope is enough; one set of nuts and small cams is plenty for them (July-August).
Drifting off the easy line on the second pitch leads onto a crack around 5.6 (late July).

In late May an extra short rappel was needed to reach the top of the second pitch before the last double-rope rappel; the sling there hung from a boulder that shifts under load, so back it up on solid blocks below.

notes: West Ridge is listed as needing a track although the stored route has points; the chosen aid is a fresh July 2026 round trip. Track 2004997 (Aug 2022) is a Stuart + Sherpa link-up and was not used for any route. No harvested track exists for East Ridge, North Ridge or the NE routes (only unsuccessful or link-up). Our summit pin matches Peakbagger's surveyed point (<10 m).
